name: VectorFFT
workload: 1D complex-to-complex FP64 interleaved out-of-place, every length N=2..4096, single thread; also 2D/3D power-of-two planes/volumes
claimed_speedup: 1D: 1.29x median over MKL across N=2..4,096 (best 7.04x at N=89; powers of two 1.13x median, 75% at/above parity); 2D 1.34x median over 159 planes; 3D 1.55x median over 1,288 volumes (README)
tradeoffs: x86 only (AVX2/AVX-512); FFT kernels generated by an OCaml DAG compiler; pure C API with wisdom planner
caveats: First-party numbers; gauntlet harness is public but compiler flags were not visible in README; very new repo with few users; MKL is slightly beaten on pow2 (1.13x) but only 75% of pow2 cells at parity; FFTW not compared in the README section opened.
found_via: WebSearch: 'arXiv FFT implementation outperforms FFTW and Intel MKL open source github'

name: VkFFT
workload: Batched 1D FFTs of all lengths 2..4096 (500MB-1GB systems), double precision, on Nvidia A100 and AMD MI250; Rader/Bluestein prime sizes; zero-padded multidimensional
claimed_speedup: Paper: near-peak 1.3TB/s on A100 where cuFFT is lower; superior to rocFFT across tested sizes; up to 2x for multidimensional transforms with zero-padding; Rader faster than cuFFT direct multiplication (per paper; per-size numbers are in figures)
tradeoffs: GPU only (Vulkan/CUDA/HIP/OpenCL/Level Zero/Metal); header-only, runtime kernel compilation; C API usable from C++
caveats: Baseline is GPU vendor libraries, not FFTW/MKL (FFTW only used as FP128 accuracy reference); speedup numbers are in figures not text; claimed only on A100/MI250.
found_via: WebSearch: 'arXiv VkFFT Vulkan FFT library performance comparison cuFFT rocFFT'

name: TurboFFT
workload: GPU FFTs on NVIDIA A100 and Tesla T4, fault-tolerance on and off
claimed_speedup: Up to 300% faster than cuFFT on certain sizes (especially small problems < 2 MB); 7-15% overhead with online fault tolerance (arXiv abstract/Figure 1)
compiler_and_flags: GCC 11.2+, CUDA 11.6-12.0 (repo requirements; flags not stated)
tradeoffs: NVIDIA GPU only; adds algorithm-based fault tolerance; research prototype
caveats: arXiv preprint (peer-review status not confirmed); best-case 'up to' figure; baseline is cuFFT not FFTW/MKL; repo has run_A100.sh/run_T4.sh reproduction scripts but I did not verify flags.
found_via: WebSearch: 'arXiv FFT implementation outperforms FFTW and Intel MKL open source github'

name: tcFFT
workload: Batched 1D and 2D half-precision FFTs on NVIDIA tensor cores, V100 and A100
claimed_speedup: 1.29x-3.24x faster than cuFFT on V100, 1.10x-3.03x on A100 (arXiv abstract)
tradeoffs: FP16 only, tensor-core GPUs only, 1D/2D only; GPL-3.0
caveats: Half precision accuracy tradeoff versus cuFFT; baseline is cuFFT not FFTW/MKL; the repo link was found via search results, and the paper abstract page does not state code link.
found_via: WebSearch: 'tensor core FFT tcFFT OR FFT GPU faster than cuFFT github open source paper'

name: FFTS (The Fastest Fourier Transform in the South)
workload: Single-precision FFT of various sizes, SSE; user-posted comparison in GitHub issue
claimed_speedup: On Core i7-870 (SSE4.2, no AVX) FFTS 1.11x-1.88x faster than FFTW across sizes (issue #28); but on i5-3340M (AVX) FFTW is faster for N>=64 and FFTS 30-50% slower
tradeoffs: Runtime dynamic code generation (disable with --disable-dynamic-code); SSE/NEON; no AVX path
caveats: Win is only on pre-AVX CPUs and reverses on AVX hardware; author says not touched for many years and points to forks (linkotec/ffts, ValveSoftware/ffts); license not visible on the pages I opened (believed BSD, unverified); evidence is a user comment.
found_via: WebSearch: 'FFT library AVX-512 outperforms FFTW github open source paper faster than FFTW' (issue #28 result)

name: KFR (DFT module)
baseline: FFTW (also Intel MKL/IPP in benchmark suite)
workload: 1D double-precision DFT, powers of two 16..16,777,216, primes 17..127, small composites 18..119, random sizes 120..30,720,000
claimed_speedup: README: 'DFT performance is on par with the most performant implementation currently available'; results are charts only, no numbers in text
stars_or_usage: 1.9k stars; used by LIGO/KAGRA ROOT add-on (arXiv 2503.14292 benchmarks KFR vs FFTW)
tradeoffs: GPL-2+ or commercial dual license; needs C++20 and Clang 16+/GCC 11+/MSVC 2022; SSE/AVX/AVX-512/NEON
caveats: Claim is 'on par', not clearly faster; numbers only in images; benchmark code at https://github.com/kfrlib/fft-benchmark (MIT) was opened but run configuration not extracted; last_commit is the v7.0.1 release month per README, not a commit date.
found_via: WebSearch: 'pocketfft OR ducc0 FFT benchmark vs FFTW MKL paper' (kfrlib/fft-benchmark result)
